definitions.short: literally, to load up (on the back of man or beast), i.e. to start early in the morning
definitions.usage: (arise, be up, get (oneself) up, rise up) early (betimes), morning.
definitions.full: H7925. shakam [ שָׁכַם ] verb Hiph`il denominative start, rise, early (properly load backs of beasts for day's journey); — Perfect 3masculine singular consecutive וְהִשְׁכִּים 2Sam 15:2 ; Job 1:5 , etc.; Imperfect 3masculine singular וַיַּשְׁכֵּם Gen 19:27 +, 2 masculine singular תְּשְׁכִּים Judg 9:33 , etc.; Imperative הַשְׁכֵּם Exod 8:16 +; Infinitive absolute הַשְׁכֵּם Jer 7:25 +, כֵּים - 44:4 ; Prov 27:14 , erroneous אַשְׁכֵּים Jer 25:3 (Ges § 53 K); Participle מַשְׁכִּים Hosea 6:4 +, etc., — rise early, make an early start , of journey (Hexateuch only J E); לְדַרְכְּכֶם Judg 19:9 (+ מָחָר ), compare Cant 7:13; + verb of going Gen 19:2 (J), standing 2Sam 15:2 (compare Dr), encamping Judg 7:1 , etc.; + infinitive 1Sam 15:12 (compare Dr), 29:11 ; 2Kin 6:15 ( לָקוּם ), קוּם מַשְׁכִּימֵי Psa 127:3 (opposed to שֶׁבֶת מְאַחֲרֵי ); usually with בַּבֹּקֶר Gen 19:27 (J; אֶלהַֿמָּקוֺם ), 1Sam 29:10 (twice in verse) + 27 t., + (hyperbole) יִרְדֹּ֑פוּ בַבּ ׳מַשְׁכִּימֵי שֵׁכָר Isa 5:11 (|| בֵנֶּשֶׁף מְאַחֲרֵי ); with מִמָּחֳרָת Exod 32:6 (E), Judg 6:28 3 t.; with הַשַּׁחַר בַּעֲלוֺת Josh 6:15 (J), 1 Samuel 19:26; וַיֵּצְאוּ וַיַּשְׁכִּימוּ וַיְמַהֲרוּ 8:14 (J) they made a quick and early start; and went out ; Infinitive absolute (Ges § 113s ) as adverb ׳הַשׁ וְהַעֲרֵב 1Sam 17:16 at early morning and at evening ; especially of ׳י , in Jeremiah: וְדַבֵּר ׳הַשׁ = speaking early and often Jer 7:13 ; 35:14 and (of Jeremiah) 25:3 , compare 11:7 ; 32:33 ; often ׳הַשׁ וְשָׁלוֺחַ = sending early and often 7:25 ; 24:4 ; 26:5 ; 29:19 ; 35:14 ; 44:4 , also 2Chr 36:15 ; so verb finite הִשְׁחִיתוּ הִשְׁכִּימוּ , Zeph 3:7 = with eagerness they corrupted (Ges § 120g ); participle מַשְׁ ׳כַּטַּל הֹלֵךְ Hosea 6:4 like the dew departing early , 13:3 (Ges ib .). — 1Sam 9:26 read וַיִּשְׁכַּב , see שׁכב
definitions.rootNote: a primitive root; properly, to incline (the shoulder to a burden); but used only as denominative from 7926 ;
